**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity, confidence 0.90)**

**What the document says**
- **§ General Provisions (c) ASSIGNMENT (p0149):** blanket prohibition on Licensee assignment/sublicense/transfer without Licensor's prior written consent — no reasonableness standard, no affiliate carve-out, no M&A/successor carve-out, and no reciprocal restriction on Licensor (so Licensor could assign to one of our competitors).
- **Article XX(a) (p0134):** on any Change of Control of Licensee, the Agreement and *all* of our rights and licenses **automatically terminate** unless Licensor consents in advance in writing; and Licensor is *deemed* reasonable in refusing if the acquirer competes with Licensor or if Licensor merely "believes" its interests would be adversely affected.

Together these sit at the playbook **walk-away** line (blanket customer assignment bar with no M&A carve-out *plus* a vendor exit on our change of control).

**Redline (validated, ok:true)**
1. p0149 — mutual assignment right without consent to an Affiliate or successor in a merger/acquisition/sale of substantially all assets or equity; Licensor may not assign to a Licensee competitor; other assignments require mutual consent "not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed."
2. p0149 — replaced the broken cross-reference to "Section 13.4(a)" with a statement that a Change of Control of Licensee is not an assignment and gives Licensor no termination, suspension or re-pricing right.
3. p0134 — deleted the automatic-termination/consent/competitor-veto trigger while preserving the "CHANGE OF CONTROL" definition that follows (it is referenced elsewhere).

**Also worth noting for a separate rule:** Article XXII (p0139) gives Licensor a 5-business-day **right of first refusal** over any sale of substantially all assets or merger of Licensee — a further constraint on our M&A that I did not touch under this rule but that our deal team should consider deleting.
